sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:1
items.html: The form of spiritual time is thoroughly explained below in Inner Observation, at its end, in the passage beginning “It still remains.”

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:2
items.html: That is, the light that expands from the self of the Creator. Know that all the names and appellations that appear in the wisdom of Kabbalah are not in the self of the Creator whatsoever, but only in the light that expands from His self. However, about His self we have no word or utterance at all, for this is the rule: anything that we do not attain, we do not know by name. Remember this and do not stumble.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:3
items.html: Seemingly, this is very perplexing: is it not speaking here of the time before the worlds were created? If so, what reality is there here that the upper light needs to fill? The thing is that all the worlds and all the souls that exist and that are destined to be created, with all that befalls them until the end of their correction, are all already included in Ein Sof [infinity], in all their glory and in all their fullness. Thus, we must discern two principles in the overall reality before us. The first principle: the discernment of how they are fixed and exist in Ein Sof, in all their completeness and glory. The second principle: as they are arranged, cascade, and are renewed before us after the first restriction, in the five worlds called Adam Kadmon, Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira, Assiya, as written below. And this is what the ARI says, that the upper light, which extends from His self, “had filled all of reality,” meaning the overall reality of the first principle, from the discernment of how they are arranged and exist in Ein Sof, which precedes the restriction. He tells us that the upper light filled them completely, until no vacant place was left in them where it would be possible to add any completeness or correction whatsoever (and study Inner Observation here well).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:4
items.html: Meaning, before the worlds were created, when there was only Ein Sof alone, as above, there was no “vacant place” there, that is, a place of deficiency that would be fit to receive the discernment of corrections. For the upper light filled that place, leaving no room for the lower ones to distinguish themselves in it by adding something to its completeness. Rather, only by reason of the restriction that took place, as written below, was a discernment of deficiency then newly made, and a vacant place for corrections came into being. But do not err in thinking that the book speaks of a corporeal place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:5
items.html: This does not refer to corporeal air whatsoever; rather, there is a discernment of spiritual light that is called so. For there are two discernments of light in every complete Partzuf, called light of Hochma and light of Hassadim. Light of Hochma is the discernment of the self of the Partzuf, that is, the discernment of the vitality in it. Light of Hassadim is only a light that clothes the light of Hochma in the Partzuf, since the light of Hochma cannot clothe in the Partzuf unless it first clothes in light of Hassadim. However, at times, when the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] are in a time of Katnut [smallness/infancy], they have only light of Hassadim. Know that this light of Hassadim is called by the name “air” or “Ruach” [wind], and when it is by itself, without light of Hochma, it is called by the name “empty air,” meaning that it is empty of the light of Hochma and therefore waits for the light of Hochma to expand within it and fill it. And the ARI tells us that before the worlds were created, that is, in Ein Sof, this discernment of empty air did not exist in reality at all, since there is not the slightest deficiency there, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:6
items.html:
In order to explain this word, you must first know what the essence of a spiritual vessel is. It is that, since the emanated being receives the abundance of its vitality from the Emanator, it necessarily has a will and a yearning to receive this abundance from Him. And know that this measure of will and yearning is the entirety of all the matter in the emanated being, so that everything in the emanated being apart from this matter is no longer attributed to the discernment of its matter, but to the discernment of its abundance, which it receives from the Emanator. Moreover, this matter is what measures the Gadlut [greatness/adulthood] and the measure of the level of every emanated being, every Partzuf, and every Sefira. For the expansion of the upper light from the Emanator is certainly without measure or size; rather, it is only the emanated being that sets a measure on the abundance by its own power, because it receives neither less nor more than the measure of its desire and its will to receive. This is the criterion that applies in spirituality, since coercion does not apply there, and everything depends on the will. Therefore, we call this “will to receive” the vessel of reception of the emanated being. It is regarded as the discernment of its matter, because of which it left the category of the Emanator to be called by the name “emanated being,” since it is defined by such a kind of matter as is not found in the Emanator in the slightest, for the will to receive absolutely does not apply in the Emanator — for from whom would He receive? Understand this.
Below we shall explain that there are four degrees in this matter, from Katnut [smallness/infancy] to the Gadlut of reception, and that the fourth degree, which is the discernment of the Gadlut of reception, found in its completeness only in Ein Sof, before the worlds were created — it is only upon her that the secret of the restriction took place. And it will be explained below that she was emptied of all the abundance she had had in relation to Ein Sof, and remained in the discernment of a vacant “space.” This is the ARI’s intention when he says that before the world was created, that is, in Ein Sof, there was no discernment of this vacant “space” there, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:7
items.html: That is, there is nothing at all to add to it through the deeds of the lower ones.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:8
items.html: The matter of Rosh [head] and Sof [end] will be explained below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:9
items.html: Meaning, there are no degrees of small and great in it; rather, everything is even, as written below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:10
items.html: That is, there is no refinement and coarseness there, by which the degrees are arranged and discerned. For these discernments came into being in the worlds only with the innovation of the restriction, which will be explained below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:11
items.html: We should ask: since we have no attainment whatsoever in Ein Sof, how then do we know Him by name? After all, every name indicates an attainment, which we attain in Him according to the indication and meaning of that name, as is known. And one cannot answer that the name Ein Sof indicates only the negation of attainment, for then we should have called Him by the name “Unattainable.” The thing is that this name shows us the entire discernment that exists between Ein Sof and all the worlds below Him. It is that the discernment of the restriction that was made after Ein Sof — in every place where this force is aroused, it restricts the light there, and by this that illumination concludes and reaches its end. Therefore, every end and conclusion that exists in every illumination and in every Partzuf extends only from the force of the restriction. Moreover, by reason of that end and conclusion, all the HaVaYot and their fillings, and all the kinds of changes that are found in the worlds, emerge and are renewed. And since this matter of the restriction is not there in Ein Sof, the matter of end and conclusion does not apply there; therefore, it is called by the name “Ein Sof” [no end], to indicate that there is no discernment of end and conclusion there whatsoever. With this it is understood that this light is simple and completely even, for one depends on the other, as written.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:12
items.html:
One should not wonder how a will is discerned in Ein Sof, who is higher than any notion, to the point of saying “it arose in His simple will,” etc. For you will understand this with what was explained above, that in every emanated being there is necessarily a will to receive its abundance from the Emanator; study it there well. Only, in Ein Sof it is a “simple will,” in the secret of “He and His Name are One,” as written in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, Chapter 1, and likewise in the words of the ARI below. For the “light” in Ein Sof is called “He,” and the “will to receive” in Ein Sof is called “His Name,” and the two of them are in the secret of the simple oneness, with no separation whatsoever between them.
However, one must not liken the separation and the oneness spoken of here to separation and oneness in corporeal concepts, which separate by way of motion, by distance of place and closeness of place, for the spiritual essence does not occupy any place at all, as is known. Indeed, know that separation in spiritual things occurs only through the occurrence of “disparity of form” alone. Thus, if one spiritual thing acquires an additional form that differs from the form it has, that spiritual thing has thereby gone out of the discernment of “one” into two separate discernments, which move away from each other according to the oppositeness that is in those two forms. And just as corporeal essences move away from and join with one another by way of distance of place and closeness of place, so spiritual essences are separated and joined according to the changing of form and the equivalence of form: the disparity of form separates them from one another, and the equivalence of form attaches them to one another. Remember this, for this is the first key to the wisdom.
Now you will understand the secret of “He and His Name are One” mentioned above, and the matter of the simple oneness about which we are so precise in Ein Sof, for this oneness is of the wonders of His omnipotence. For it was explained above in Inner Light (item 6) that the difference between the Emanator and the emanated being came about because of the form of the “will to receive” that exists in the emanated being and not in the Emanator; by reason of that disparity of form, the emanated being was separated from the Emanator and acquired a name of its own, to be called “emanated being” and not “Emanator”; study it there well.
And according to what has been explained, there is room to err and think that the light of Ein Sof, called “He,” is not completely attached to Ein Sof, called “His Name,” that is, the “will to receive” the abundance and the light called “He.” For the upper light that extends from His self, called “He,” its entire nature is only to bestow, and it has nothing at all of the form of the will to receive, as explained there. This is not so with Ein Sof, called “His Name,” which has the will to receive and is therefore different from the upper light, which has no will to receive whatsoever, as explained, and it is known that disparity of form makes separation. This is what Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer and the ARI below tell us: that it is not so at all; rather, He and His Name are One in simple oneness, with no difference whatsoever between them. And although there is necessarily some disparity of form between them — between “He” and “His Name” — as explained, nevertheless it does not act there at all. And although we do not understand this, it is nevertheless so beyond any doubt. And about this they said that in Ein Sof no thought grasps Him at all, this matter being above our intellect (continued in the adjacent item).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:13
items.html:
Meaning, you already know the secret of “He and His Name are One”: although there is disparity of form in the discernment of the will to receive included in Ein Sof, nevertheless this makes no difference there between it and the upper light; rather, they are in simple oneness. And with all that, this form we have spoken of became the reason and the cause for the creation of the worlds and “to bring the perfection of His deeds, His names, and appellations to light,” as the ARI says here. For through the creation of the worlds and their cascading down to this world, in which the possibility was made and newly brought about of giving room for work in Torah and Mitzvot not in order “to receive” but only “to bestow” contentment upon the Maker, the souls are then able to invert the form of the will to receive in them, which separates them from the Emanator, into the form of a will to bestow, that is, to receive from the Emanator in order to bestow contentment upon Him, since He wishes so, as I have written below, item 90; see there. This is the equivalence of form with the Emanator, which is called adhesion and unification, as above, the passage beginning “However.” For then they have already been stripped of the form of the will to receive and have acquired the form of the will to bestow, which is the form of the Emanator Himself. And you already know that equivalence of form makes spiritual things one; therefore, the worlds then return to their former state, as written further on.
And this is what the ARI says: “When it arose in His simple will to create,” etc. “Arose” means that it was elevated in refinement and adhesion by diminishing and restricting the measure of the will to receive imprinted in it, in order to equalize its form with the upper light. And although the will to receive in Ein Sof, called Malchut of Ein Sof or “His Name,” as above, had no deficiency whatsoever in its adhesion with the upper light because of the disparity of form in it, as said, nevertheless it adorned itself to equalize its form with the upper light and to depart at least from this Gadlut [greatness/adulthood] of the will to receive, which is called phase four in it, in order to adhere more to the upper light. For closeness of form makes adhesion, as above, the passage beginning “However.” This is what is expressed by the word “arose”: that Malchut of Ein Sof, which is the secret of the “simple will,” rose and adhered to the upper light, that is, she diminished her will to receive, as explained.
And this is what the ARI says: “And behold, then He restricted Himself,” etc. For it has already been explained (above, item 6) that the entire measure of the abundance, the light, and the level of the emanated being is measured by the measure of the will to receive in it; study it there well. Therefore, since the above-mentioned Malchut of Ein Sof restricted herself and diminished the will to receive in her, the light and the abundance consequently departed because of the diminution of the will. This is the matter of the restriction: the elevation of the will caused the departure of the light and the abundance from there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:14
items.html:
This is seemingly perplexing: since there is no Rosh [head] and Sof [end] there, how can there be a middle? Moreover, are we dealing with a corporeal matter that occupies a place? The thing is that it has already been explained that in Ein Sof, too, there is necessarily a discernment of the will to receive, only in the secret of a “simple will,” meaning that there is no discernment of degrees of small and great in it, as above, since the will to receive that is there is not regarded as a discernment of disparity of form that makes any separation whatsoever. Hence, it has no inferiority whatsoever with respect to the upper light. And you must know that the upper light is compelled to expand through four degrees until it reveals this will to receive in the emanated being in its fixed and permanent completeness.
And the reason for the necessity of the four degrees is that the above-mentioned will to receive is included immediately with the expansion of the light from the root, for by this it is discerned that the light has gone out of the Emanator and acquired a name of its own, that is, an expansion from the Emanator. As long as this disparity of form of the will to receive is not included in it, it is certainly still the discernment of the Emanator, and not the discernment of an expansion that is detached and goes out of the Emanator, for in spirituality no difference can be depicted except through disparity of form (as above, item 6, see there; and see Inner Observation here). However, as long as there is no disclosure of this will by the power of the emanated being itself, it is not yet fixed in the emanated being. That is, the emanated being must yearn to receive the abundance, for then it is discerned that the will to receive has been revealed by the power of the emanated being itself. And this yearning cannot be except at a time when it does not have the abundance, for only then is it possible for it to yearn after it, in a way that the “will to receive” is revealed in it by its own power, and then the vessels of reception are completed permanently. You must know one more thing: every expansion of light from the Emanator, just as it is comprised of the discernment of a will to receive, as said, must also be comprised of the discernment of a will to bestow. Otherwise, the Emanator and the emanated being would be in the discernment of oppositeness of form, which is complete separation, for oppositeness of form would distance them from one another as the east is far from the west. Therefore, every light that expands from the Emanator must also be comprised of the discernment of the will to bestow, so that there will be nearness of form between the Emanator and the emanated being. And when this will to bestow is revealed in the emanated being, a great light extends to it from the Emanator, related to the arousal of this will, and this light is everywhere called light of Hassadim. However, the first expansion from the Emanator, in which the will to receive is included, as explained above, is everywhere called light of Hochma, or the light of the self. Remember these two kinds of lights well. And know that the second light, which is light of Hassadim, is much lower than the first light, which is light of Hochma, since it is extended through the intensification and the arousal of the emanated being by its own power, because it wishes to equalize its form with the Emanator; for this reason, it intensifies and is aroused to the discernment of the will to bestow, as explained. This is not so with the first expansion, which is light of Hochma: it extends directly from the Emanator, and the emanated being has no part in its extension. Hence, it is incomparably higher than it, and therefore the “light of Hochma” is regarded as the self and the vitality of the emanated being, while the “light of Hassadim” is regarded only as the discernment of a light of corrections, for the completion of the emanated being.
Now you will understand the four phases and the degrees that must be present in every emanated being, as above. For at first the light expands and goes out of the Emanator, as above, in the discernment of light of Hochma, in which only the “will to receive” is included; this is phase one. Afterwards, the discernment of the will to bestow intensifies in this light, and it draws light of Hassadim, as above; this intensification is regarded as phase two. Afterwards, this light of Hassadim expands in a great expansion, whose meaning will be explained below; this is phase three. And after the above three phases have emerged and been revealed in their fullness, the force of the will to receive included in the first expansion is aroused once more and again draws the light of Hochma. This is the ultimate completeness of the permanence of the will to receive in the Partzuf, since it is revealed in the discernment of yearning. That is, at a time when there was no light of Hochma in the Partzuf, but only light of Hassadim, namely after the above phase three, the emanated being had the possibility of yearning to receive the light of Hochma; this yearning fixes the will to receive in it and completes its vessels of reception, which was not so in the first expansion (as above, in the passage beginning “And the reason for the necessity”; see there). Therefore, the vessels of reception are completed only in this phase four, which is also called the second intensification. And after the completion of this phase four in Ein Sof, the restriction occurred in her, which means the departure of the will to receive from this phase four, and this caused the departure of the light of Ein Sof from there (as above, page 4, the passage beginning “And this is what the ARI says, And behold”; study it there well).
Thus, the four phases that must be present in every emanated being have been explained: phase one is called the first expansion, or Hochma; phase two is called the first intensification, or Bina; phase three is called the second expansion, or Zeir Anpin; and phase four is called the second intensification, or Malchut. The two expansions are regarded as males, since they are the discernment of the abundance that extends from the Emanator: the first expansion is the abundance of the light of Hochma, and the second expansion is the abundance of light of Hassadim. And the two intensifications are two females, since they are the discernment of the arousal of the emanated being and the intensification of the will by its own power: the first intensification is the arousal in the emanated being toward the “will to bestow,” which becomes a root for the light of Hassadim, as above; and the second intensification is the arousal in the emanated being toward the “will to receive,” which becomes the discernment of a vessel of reception for the Partzuf, in all the desired completeness. It is this that is everywhere called phase four.
This phase four is what is called the middle point in Ein Sof, and it is she whom the ARI meant when he said, “restricted Himself in the middle point in Him.” She is called so because she is the vessel of reception for the light of Ein Sof, which is entirely without measure and without boundary. Therefore, her existence is discerned as a point in the interior and in the middle of that light, while the light surrounds her and is attached to her all around, without measure. For only in this way is it possible for her to hold an upper light without any size and without any measure. This is not so with the vessels of reception from the restriction downward, that is, in the lower emanated beings, in whom the vessels of reception are discerned as holding their light within their internality and their interior. That is, the walls of the vessels, which are the secret of the four phases in them, set a boundary and a measure on the light within them, and this is because of the coarseness in the vessels, as written below. This is not so in Ein Sof, where the light and the vessel are in simple oneness, in the secret of “He and His Name are One” (as above, item 30, the passage beginning “And according”); therefore, the vessel does not limit the light that it holds at all, and hence the light in it is in the discernment of Ein Sof. Thus, the secret of the middle point in Ein Sof has been thoroughly explained: it does not speak whatsoever of the discernment of a corporeal place and area in tangible measures; rather, the phase four included in Ein Sof is called so on account of her simple oneness with the upper light, as explained.
And the matter of the restriction that was made in this middle point has already been explained above, item 40, the passage beginning “And this is what the ARI says”; study it there well.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:15
items.html: Spiritual distance was explained in item 30, the passage beginning “However”; see there. It was also explained that in Ein Sof there was no distance whatsoever between the middle point, which is the secret of the vessel, and the light; see there. However, after He restricted the light from within the middle point, her disparity of form from the light was thereby revealed. For the upper light has nothing at all of the discernment of the will to receive, but the point is in the discernment of a “will to receive,” which differs from the light, as above. And since their forms have changed from one another, they are far from one another by the measure of the difference of this change, as above. And this is what the ARI says: “and moved away,” etc.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:16
items.html: The above four phases are also called four sides. And the ARI tells us that although the restriction was only in the middle point, as above, which is phase four, the light nevertheless departed from all four phases, since the matter of “part” does not apply in spirituality; therefore, it departed from the three phases as well.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:17
items.html: This was already explained above, in item 4 and in item 5; see there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:18
items.html:
Meaning, without a discernment of degrees of small and great. And one should not ask: since the disparity of form that is in the middle point has already been revealed through the departure of the light from her, it necessarily follows that the smaller measures, one smaller than the other, were also recognized because of this, in the disparity of form within the three preceding degrees — where phase three, for example, is more refined than the middle point, since the measure of the will to receive in her is less than in phase four; likewise phase two is more refined than phase three, since the measure of the will in her is less than in phase three; and phase one is the most refined of all, since the measure of the will to receive in her is the least of all, and therefore her disparity of form is not as noticeable as in them. Thus, there is a discernment of degrees of small and great here, so how does the ARI say that the restriction was even around the point? The answer is that the restriction did not make the middle point into the discernment of “Sof” [end]. That is, had the light departed from the point by reason of the disparity of form in her, she would then certainly have become, because of this, the discernment of “Sof,” which means the most inferior degree, below which there is nothing lower in inferiority. We would then also have to discern the three preceding phases as more important than the middle point, in the manner of one above the other. But it was not so, for the restriction was not made because of the disparity of form in the point — that is impossible, since we are still dealing with Malchut of Ein Sof, where there is no disparity of form whatsoever between her and the light, as the two of them are in simple oneness, in the secret of “He and His Name are One,” as above. Rather, the restriction was made only in the secret of “it arose in His simple will to create the worlds,” etc., as above (item 40, the passage beginning “Meaning”; see there). This means that He desired that equivalence of form which is destined to be revealed through the creation of the worlds, namely the form of reception in order to bestow contentment upon the Maker, in which there is a very lofty, surpassing merit: on the one hand, it is complete bestowal, for the entire will is only to bestow contentment upon the Maker and nothing at all for one’s own needs; hence, its form is completely equal to the upper light of the Emanator, and it is found to be attached to Him in the utmost adhesion. And on the other hand, it is able to deepen and enlarge its vessels of reception without end and without limit, for now the form of reception does not make any disparity of form, since it comes from the will to bestow. This is as our sages said (in Tractate Kiddushin, page 7a), that with an important man, if she gave the betrothal money and he said, “Behold, you are betrothed to me,” she is betrothed. And although it is written in the Torah, “and gives it in her hand,” meaning that the husband must give the betrothal money, nevertheless, since he is an important man, this pleasure, that he receives from her, is regarded as actual giving; study it there well. Thus, “reception in order to bestow” is giving and not reception. For this reason, an important man who receives money from her is like one who gives her money, and it is as written in the Torah, “and gives it in her hand,” because he receives only in order to bestow contentment upon the woman, that she may be honored by his reception.
It follows from what has been explained that the entire primary cause of the restriction was only the desire for the new form of “reception in order to bestow,” which is destined to be revealed through the creation of the worlds (as above, item 40, the passage beginning “Meaning”), but not at all because of any coarseness that He felt in the middle point, for there was no coarseness and no change there whatsoever, as above. Therefore, the middle point did not become the discernment of “Sof” because of the restriction. Hence, it is not at all possible to discern a matter of small and great, and this is what the ARI says, that the restriction was completely even.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:19
items.html: Meaning, some image was necessarily made here because of the restriction. And although the restriction was even (as thoroughly explained in the adjacent item above), and not because of disparity of form, nevertheless, after the restriction and the departure of the light from that middle point, it became revealed that the upper light is not fit to adhere to her because of the form of the Gadlut [greatness/adulthood] of reception found in her. And once this was revealed, she fell from the degree she had had in Ein Sof. If so, she is already regarded as the discernment of “Sof” [end], which means coarseness below which there is nothing lower: for this reason only this middle point remained a vacant space and is no longer fit for the clothing of the light (as above, item 6, the passage beginning “In order”), while the three phases that precede her in merit and in refinement are still fit for the clothing of the light in them even after the restriction. And with all that, we explained above (in the adjacent item) that she did not become the discernment of “Sof,” for the above reason; see there. This is what the ARI is precise in saying, “that the place of that space was round on all its sides,” meaning not an actual “Sof,” but like the end in a “round image,” whose end is at its center. Thus, you should picture these four phases as four circles one within the other, like the layers of an onion, where the central circle is phase four, phase three surrounds her, phase two surrounds it, and phase one surrounds it. In this way, no discernment of above and below, right and left, is discerned among them. For phase one, for example, which in its first half surrounds above them all, in its second half is found surrounding below them all, and so with the other phases. If so, there is no above and below here, and likewise no right and left, so that none of them has any merit over another, and they are all completely even. The reason has already been explained (in the adjacent item): because the cause of the restriction was not disparity of form; study it there well. And this is what the ARI is precise in saying, “round on all its sides, completely even.” Understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:20
items.html: This has already been explained above, in the adjacent item.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:21
items.html: This means that had there been a discernment of above and below, right and left, there, it would have been expressed in the image of the square, which has these four sides, which are the appellations of the above four phases. But it was not so; rather, it was in the image of the circle, which does not have these discernments, as above, in the adjacent item.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 1:1:22
items.html: It indicates a degree that has only three phases, in which phase four is missing; that is, three sides: above, right, and left, while the lower side is missing there. This is called the image of the triangle.
